title: The Hyatt Walkway Collapse: One Phone Call Doubled the Load
cta: Which link in the chain should have stopped it? Tell us in the comments

facts.label: Year the Hyatt Regency walkways collapsed
Day of July 1981 the walkways collapsed
Hour of the collapse (p.m.), approximately 7:05 p.m.
Minutes past the hour of the collapse (approximately 7:05 p.m.)
People left dead by the collapse (NBS executive summary)
Ultimate capacity of the original continuous-rod connection, percent of that expected under the Kansas City Building Code (approximately)
How many times the rod change multiplied the load on the fourth-floor box beam-hanger rod connections (essentially doubled)
Year ASCE adopted the policy assigning responsibility for steel connection design, including connections, to the engineer of record (October 1985)
Year the Hyatt Regency Kansas City opened for business (July 1980)
Storeys of the hotel's tower section (a 40-story tower)
Height of the atrium, about 50 ft (15 m)
Crowd in the atrium at 7:00 p.m., low end of the newspaper estimate (1500 to 2000), as summarised in the NBS report
Crowd in the atrium at 7:00 p.m., high end of the newspaper estimate (1500 to 2000), as summarised in the NBS report
Credible estimate of combined second and fourth floor walkway occupancy at the time of collapse, from the videotape
Maximum load on a fourth floor box beam-hanger rod connection at the time of collapse, percent of the ultimate capacity expected of a connection designed under the Kansas City Building Code
How much heavier the actual walkway dead load (self-weight) was than the nominal dead load (approximately 8 percent)
Depth in inches of each of the two steel channels welded toe to toe into a box beam (8-inch channels)
Minutes past 7 p.m. when the band returned from its break and began to play for the dance contest (7:04 p.m., newspaper chronology in the NBS report)
People injured in the collapse (NBS executive summary)
Associate engineers the engineer of record was responsible for (roughly 10, each supervising six or seven projects)
Professional engineers whose licences the Missouri Board revoked after the investigation
Hanger rods suspending the fourth floor walkway from the atrium roof framing
Years ASCE suspended the engineer of record from membership
Minutes past 7 p.m. when the Kansas City Fire Department dispatcher received the first call for help (7:08 p.m., newspaper chronology in the NBS report)
Minutes past 7 p.m. when the call went out for cutting tools (7:19 p.m., newspaper chronology in the NBS report)
Minutes past 7 p.m. when the call went out for a forklift (7:23 p.m., newspaper chronology in the NBS report)

beats.say: Kansas City, {fact1}. Two steel walkways hang over a crowded hotel lobby, one directly above the other.

params.place: under the fourth-floor walkway of the Hyatt Regency atrium, at night

moments.what: the date and place caption types on over the amber-lit nut under the upper walkway
the rod glints as the camera slides back along the box beam
the camera pulls back: both walkways in frame, rails and glass catching the light
the dance-floor lights pulse on below
the full atrium opens: roof trusses, balconies, tables and chairs
a dashed line drops from the upper walkway to the lower

beats.say: On the upper walkway, one nut and washer are holding far more than they were ever meant to.

params.place: inside the fourth-floor box beam, cut away

moments.what: the beam's near face cuts away to show the rods inside
the camera pushes onto the nut under the bottom flange
load arrows press down onto the washer
the steel warms grey to amber around the nut
a mono label types on: FOURTH-FLOOR BOX BEAM

beats.say: At about {fact4} past {fact3} in the evening, the beam around that nut tears open.

params.place: the fourth-floor box beam, close

moments.what: a clock card slides in with the time
stress climbs from amber to red, the music falls away
the weld seam glows and pulses
sub-boom: the seam rips, the nut pulls through, sparks fall

beats.say: In seconds, both walkways are on the floor.

params.place: the atrium from high above, after the collapse

moments.what: seen from the roof trusses, dust rolls across the lobby floor
the two fallen walkways lie stacked, lit in red outline
the empty hanger rods swing from the roof

beats.say: Why? The investigators found the steel and the workmanship played no significant role. It was a chain of small decisions, and one of them was made over the phone.

params.place: the investigators' cause board

moments.what: the board lights up, five empty links pinned across it
a card STEEL? drops and is struck out in red
a card WORKMANSHIP? drops and is struck out
the five links light one after another
each link takes a pin
the middle link becomes a telephone handset, ringing

beats.say: This is how one small change on a drawing doubled the load, and why nobody caught it.

params.place: the engineer's drawing of the hanger, side elevation

moments.what: the one long rod on the drawing splits into two
a revision cloud draws round the split
two load arrows merge into one thick red arrow on the nut
an unticked CONNECTION CALCS line flashes on the title block

beats.say: The Hyatt Regency walkway collapse.

params.place: the atrium seen through the glass roof, at dusk

moments.what: the camera sinks through the glass roof grid
the title writes on in mono across the roof beams
the music drops to silence, then the drone returns

beats.say: The Hyatt Regency in Kansas City opened in {fact9}.

params.place: outside the hotel, the tower and the atrium, afternoon

moments.what: the chapter title THE HOTEL types on
the camera glides past the tower at an angle
the opening year lights up on the sign by the entrance

beats.say: A {fact10}-storey tower, a block of ballrooms, and between them a glass atrium about {fact11} high.

params.place: outside the hotel, the tower and the atrium, afternoon

moments.what: the tower's floor count runs up its edge
the low function block lights from inside
the atrium's glass roof catches the sun
a height marker draws up the atrium's side

beats.say: Across that atrium ran three walkways, at the second, third and fourth floors.

params.place: inside the atrium, by day

moments.what: the camera drifts in through the lobby, sunlight through the roof
three walkway edges light in turn
a label SECOND FLOOR draws to the lowest
a label THIRD FLOOR to the offset one
a label FOURTH FLOOR to the top one

beats.say: The third was set off to one side. The fourth-floor walkway ran directly above the second.

params.place: inside the atrium, by day, from the end of the walkways

moments.what: the offset third-floor walkway glows and slides a guide line to the side
the fourth-floor walkway glows
a plumb line drops from it to the second-floor walkway
the second-floor walkway glows beneath

beats.say: No columns held them up over the lobby. Each one hung from the roof on thin steel rods.

params.place: the atrium, looking up the hanger rods

moments.what: ghost columns rise under the walkway and fade out
the camera tilts up from the walkway
the roof trusses come into view
the rods light up one after another, a mono label HANGER RODS

beats.say: Why hang them? Because a walkway floating in the air looks weightless, and it keeps the lobby floor clear for crowds.

params.place: the lobby floor, low angle under the walkways

moments.what: a low shot from the lobby floor up at the walkways
the walkways seem to hover against the glass
light glides along the underside
the open floor below fills with tables and chairs

beats.say: For a year, they held. Nobody could see what was wrong with them.

params.place: the atrium as days pass, light sweeping through

moments.what: sunlight sweeps across the atrium again and again as days pass
the walkways stay still while the light moves
the camera pushes into one box beam under the upper walkway, an amber point on it

beats.say: So what was wrong from the very first day? To see it, you have to look inside one joint.

params.place: the box beam under the fourth-floor walkway, approached from outside

moments.what: the walkway's underside fills the frame
the camera slides along to the middle box beam
the beam's skin peels away to show the inside
the nut and washer are lit, a mono label THE JOINT

beats.say: Under each walkway ran steel box beams. Each one was two {fact17}-inch channels, welded toe to toe.

params.place: an empty steel shop, two channels on a bench

moments.what: the chapter title HOW IT WAS MEANT TO HOLD types on
a box beam turns on the bench
the beam splits into two C-shaped channels, the depth marked
they slide together and a weld bead runs along the seam, glowing

params.chapter: How it was meant to hold

beats.say: A rod came down from the roof, through a hole in the beam. Underneath, a nut and washer held the beam up.

params.place: the box beam at the end of a walkway

moments.what: a hanger rod descends from above
it threads through the holes in the top and bottom flange
a washer slides up and a nut spins on beneath the beam
the beam settles onto the nut, an arrow up from it

beats.say: Here is the weak spot. The rod passed through a hole drilled right where the two channels' edges met, along the weld.

params.place: the bottom of the box beam, close

moments.what: the camera slides under the beam's bottom face
the rod hole glows, drilled through the seam
the two flange edges light either side of it
the weld bead along the seam lights amber

beats.say: So the whole weight pressed down through one washer onto two thin flange lips, held together by that weld. How much could that take?

params.place: the bottom of the box beam, cut away

moments.what: a load arrow presses down the beam
the washer lights under the flange
the two flange lips flex, exaggerated
the weld bead pulses
a question mark beside the joint

beats.say: What did the engineers draw? One long rod for both walkways.

params.place: the engineers' contract drawing

moments.what: the side elevation draws on: roof, fourth-floor and second-floor beams
one continuous rod draws from the roof down
both walkway decks fill in

beats.say: It ran from the roof, through the fourth-floor beam, and straight on down through the second-floor beam.

params.place: the engineers' contract drawing

moments.what: a light runs down the rod from the roof
it passes through the upper beam
and keeps going
it reaches the lower beam's nut

beats.say: Each beam sat on its own nut, so each nut carried only its own walkway.

params.place: the two box beams on one long rod, as designed

moments.what: a load arrow drops onto the upper nut
a second arrow drops onto the lower nut
both arrows the same size, labelled ONE WALKWAY

beats.say: Was that design safe? Not quite. The investigators found it reached only about {fact6} of the strength the Kansas City code expected.

params.place: a strength gauge beside the drawing

moments.what: a strength gauge slides in beside the joint
the needle starts to climb
a label ORIGINAL DESIGN types on beside the gauge
it stops at the figure, short of the code line
the code line flashes red

beats.say: So the drawing was already short. Then, during construction, someone asked a simple question.

params.place: the engineers' office at night, a phone on the desk

moments.what: the drawing lies on the desk under a lamp
a site photo slides in next to it
the desk phone starts to ring, the handset shaking

beats.say: The steel fabricator looked at that long rod and saw a problem.

params.place: the fabricator's shop floor, the long rod on trestles

moments.what: the chapter title THE CHAIN types on, the long rod lies across the shop floor
its whole length lights
a question mark appears over its middle

beats.say: How do you put a nut halfway up a rod that long? The rod would need thread most of its length, or the nut wound all the way up.

params.place: the fabricator's shop floor, close on the rod

moments.what: a nut slides onto the bottom of the rod
a target mark at the middle
thread lines spread along the rod
the nut spins its long way up, a turn counter racing

beats.say: Two shorter rods were simpler. One from the roof to the fourth-floor beam. A second from that beam down to the second floor.

params.place: the fabricator's shop drawing

moments.what: the long rod splits in two
a short tick mark
the first rod draws from roof to upper beam
the second rod draws from the upper beam down, offset beside the first

beats.say: As reported, the fabricator asked for the change by telephone. The structural engineer agreed, on the understanding that a written request would follow.

params.place: the engineers' office, the phone call

moments.what: an AS REPORTED tag appears
the handset lifts, sound waves pulse
a FABRICATOR tag drops beside the shop drawing
a hand-written note OK slides under it
an empty request form slides in

beats.say: As reported, the written request never came.

params.place: the engineers' office, the in-tray

moments.what: the form waits in the in-tray
days flip on the desk calendar; the tray stays empty

beats.say: On paper the two joints look almost the same. They aren't.

params.place: two box beams side by side, cut away

moments.what: two cut-away box beams turn side by side
the left shows one long rod, the right two rods
both slow to the same angle
the right one's nut glows amber

beats.say: With one rod, the lower walkway hangs from the roof. With two, it hangs from the upper walkway's beam.

params.place: the load path drawing, both versions

moments.what: on the left a load line runs from the lower walkway straight to the roof
it ends at the roof
on the right the line stops at the upper beam
the upper beam lights

beats.say: Think of two climbers on one rope. Each holds the rope with their own hands. Now tie the lower climber to the upper one's harness instead.

params.place: a general principle: two climbers on a rope

moments.what: two climbers hang on one rope, drawn in outline
the rope pulls taut from the anchor
each one's grip glows
the lower climber's rope is cut and retied to the upper climber's harness
the upper grip turns amber, carrying both

beats.say: Now the nut under the upper beam carries its own walkway, and the whole walkway below it.

params.place: inside the fourth-floor box beam, cut away

moments.what: the camera pushes in on the roof rod's nut
one load arrow presses on it
a second arrow comes up the lower rod and joins it
the nut turns amber

beats.say: The load on that connection essentially doubled.

params.place: inside the fourth-floor box beam, cut away

moments.what: the two arrows merge into one thick red one
the multiplier stamps beside the nut

beats.say: So who calculated the new joint? Nobody did.

params.place: the as-built joint, turning in the dark

moments.what: the as-built joint turns, its two rods lit
a CONNECTION CALCS line types on beside it
the line reads NONE in red and the joint's outline dashes red

beats.say: The fabricator was busy, and passed the drawings to an outside detailer.

params.place: a second desk across town

moments.what: a tower of job folders grows on the fabricator's desk
the drawings slide off across the frame
they land on a second desk, tagged OUTSIDE DETAILER

beats.say: As reported, the detailer believed the two-rod joint had already been designed, so he did no calculations on it.

params.place: the detailer's desk

moments.what: an AS REPORTED tag appears
a sticky note ALREADY DESIGNED? sticks to the joint
a tick is scribbled beside the note
the calculation pad stays blank, a red line through it

beats.say: Back at the engineers' office, a technician reviewed the drawings. The joint wasn't detailed on them, and nobody calculated it.

params.place: the as-built joint, seen as the reviewers never saw it

moments.what: the joint sits small in the dark, a drawing-sheet frame round it
a checklist panel slides in: dimensions, sizes, materials ticked
the camera pushes in: the connection itself is a blank dashed circle
the CONNECTIONS line stays unticked, red

beats.say: The engineer of record made spot checks, and put his seal on the drawings.

params.place: the engineers' office, the seal

moments.what: a few red check marks dot the sheet
the engineer's seal stamps down on the title block

beats.say: How could that happen? He was responsible for about {fact20} associate engineers, each running several projects at once.

params.place: the engineers' office floor, rows of desks

moments.what: the camera pulls back over rows of desks
desk lamps light in a row, the count on the wall board
folders stack up on every desk

beats.say: Four links, each one small. And the walkways were already hanging by them when the hotel planned a party.

params.place: the atrium in the late afternoon, the walkways hanging

moments.what: four link chips appear over the atrium: weak joint, rod change, detailer, review
the chips shrink to the corner
the camera pushes along the hanger rods to the upper walkway
the dance-floor lights come on below

beats.say: So far: a joint that was already weak, a change that doubled its load, and drawings that nobody calculated. What was still missing? A crowd.

params.place: the investigators' cause board

moments.what: the weak-joint card lights
the phone-call card lights
the review card lights
an empty space on the board
the dance poster fills the space

beats.say: Friday, July {fact2}, {fact1}. A dance in the atrium.

params.place: the atrium in the early evening, set for a dance

moments.what: the chapter title THE LAST MINUTES types on; the date caption
the bandstand lights come up, the dance floor glows

beats.say: By the evening, newspapers put the crowd at {fact12} to {fact13} people.

params.place: the atrium, full tables, evening

moments.what: the lobby lamps glow brighter
a newspaper clipping card slides in, AS REPORTED
the clipping's headline underlines
every table and chair across the lobby lights warm, the estimate on the bandstand's board
the camera keeps rising over the full lobby

beats.say: Some watched from the walkways above.

params.place: the walkways from the dance floor

moments.what: the camera rises from the dance floor
the walkway rails glow warm
small lights along the rails, where people stood

beats.say: A television crew was filming. From its tape, investigators later counted about {fact14} people on the second and fourth-floor walkways.

params.place: a news camera on a tripod on the balcony

moments.what: a news camera on a tripod pans across the atrium
its viewfinder fills the frame
count marks tick along the walkways in the viewfinder
the count settles on the viewfinder

beats.say: Is that a heavy load? No. The building code expected walkways like these to carry far more people than that.

params.place: a load comparison drawn over the walkway

moments.what: a load bar for the people on the walkways
a far taller bar for what the code expected
the gap between them shades

beats.say: At {fact18} minutes past {fact3}, the band came back from its break for a dance contest.

params.place: the bandstand, close

moments.what: the lobby clock ticks
the bandstand lights flare
the dance floor tiles pulse to the beat

beats.say: One minute later, under the upper walkway, one nut was about to let go.

params.place: under the fourth-floor walkway, the lights of the dance below

moments.what: the lobby clock ticks once more
the camera rises to the upper walkway's underside
it finds the middle box beam's nut, glowing amber

beats.say: It began at the east end of the fourth-floor walkway's middle box beam.

params.place: along the underside of the fourth-floor walkway

moments.what: the chapter title THE FAILURE types on
the camera tracks along the walkway's underside
the middle box beam lights
a label MIDDLE BOX BEAM · EAST END draws to its end

beats.say: The rod held. The nut held. The beam around them did not.

params.place: inside the fourth-floor box beam, cut away

moments.what: the rod ticks green
the nut ticks green
the flange and weld around the nut flush red

beats.say: The welded seam split, the flange bent open, and the nut and washer pulled straight through.

params.place: inside the fourth-floor box beam, cut away, slowed down

moments.what: silence: the seam glows red under the nut
sub-boom: the seam rips open
the flange folds down
the nut and washer punch through, sparks and steel flecks fall

beats.say: And with one hanger gone? The others took its share, and failed one after another.

params.place: the fourth-floor walkway from the side

moments.what: the first connection lets go, the beam drops at that end
the next connections glow red in turn
each one pops in sequence along the walkway

beats.say: The fourth-floor walkway fell onto the second, and both crashed to the lobby floor.

params.place: the atrium, wide

moments.what: the upper walkway drops onto the lower
both tilt and fall
dust rises from the lobby floor

beats.say: {fact5} people died and {fact19} were injured. The federal report called it the most devastating structural collapse ever to take place in the United States.

params.place: the atrium from high above, after the collapse, dimmed

moments.what: high view, the fallen walkways in settling dust, the camera craning slowly up
the lights dim
the dust settles lower
the camera stops rising
the lights dim further
a quiet line types on: THE MOST DEVASTATING STRUCTURAL COLLAPSE
the camera keeps rising
the second line types on: EVER TO TAKE PLACE IN THE UNITED STATES · NBS

beats.say: The first call for help reached the fire department at {fact24} minutes past {fact3}. By {fact25} past, rescuers were calling for cutting tools, and by {fact26} past, a forklift.

params.place: the atrium after the collapse, emergency lights

moments.what: red and blue light washes in through the doors
the lobby clock card shows the time
the emergency lights strengthen
the clock card ticks over to the first call
work lights come on over the fallen walkways
sparks from a cutting tool at the walkway edge
a forklift's lights move in

beats.say: The third-floor walkway, hung on its own rods from the roof, stayed up.

params.place: the atrium, the third-floor walkway still hanging

moments.what: the offset walkway is lit, still in place
its rods light up to the roof
a green tick beside it

beats.say: Investigators had to answer one question. Was it the change alone, or was the joint always too weak?

params.place: the investigators' table, the evidence

moments.what: an evidence bag with a bent washer and nut lands on the table
the evidence tag swings
the shop drawing slides beside it
the original drawing slides in on the other side; a question mark between them

beats.say: The National Bureau of Standards took the case, and weighed pieces of the fallen walkways.

params.place: the National Bureau of Standards' test hall

moments.what: the chapter title WHAT THEY FOUND types on over the test hall
a walkway section rests on a floor scale
the scale's display counts up

beats.say: The decks were about {fact16} heavier than the drawings assumed. That was not enough to explain it.

params.place: the test hall, the floor scale

moments.what: a concrete core sample sits on the scale
the display shows the extra weight
a DRAWN WEIGHT line appears on the display
a small arrow on a big gauge: too small

beats.say: So they built copies of the box beam joint and pulled on them until they broke.

params.place: the test hall, a hydraulic test rig

moments.what: a box beam specimen is lowered into the rig
a row of identical specimens waits on a rack
the ram pulls the rod, the load needle climbs
the specimen's nut jerks through

beats.say: They broke the way the real ones did. The weld split, and the nut punched through.

params.place: the test rig, close on the specimen

moments.what: the specimen in close-up
the weld seam opens
the nut punches through, flecks fall

beats.say: Then they did the sums. How much was that joint carrying on the night?

params.place: a calculation sheet over the joint drawing

moments.what: a calculation sheet slides over the joint
a load arrow on the nut
a strength gauge slides in, empty

beats.say: At most, about {fact15} of what a joint built to the code should have held.

params.place: the strength gauge

moments.what: the bar fills and stops low
a mono label A JOINT BUILT TO CODE draws to the code line
the code line far above it lights
the gap between them shades red

beats.say: And here is the turn. Under the original one-rod design, those same joints would have survived that night.

params.place: the two joints side by side, original and as built

moments.what: the drawing splits in two
the one-rod joint on the left lights
the night's load arrow presses on both
the left one holds with a green tick, the right one flashes red

beats.say: The original still fell short of the code. But it would have held.

params.place: the original joint

moments.what: the left joint alone
its gauge shows the original figure, under the code line
the nut stays put, a green glow

beats.say: With two rods, the report says, from the day they were built the walkways had only minimal capacity to resist their own weight.

params.place: the investigators' report on the desk

moments.what: the real report page settles on the desk, the agency and date chips type on
the camera pushes into the abstract
the line to be marked brightens
the highlighter swipes across the line
the highlight runs on to the second line
a red underline draws under OWN WEIGHT

beats.say: For a year, people walked across a structure that could barely hold itself up.

params.place: the atrium by day, the walkways empty

moments.what: sunlight in the empty atrium again
a light passes along the walkway deck
the camera pushes in on the amber box beam

beats.say: In Missouri, the engineering board revoked the licences of {fact21} engineers involved, for gross negligence and misconduct.

params.place: the state board's table

moments.what: the chapter title WHAT CHANGED types on; two licence cards slide onto the table
each is stamped REVOKED
the second card is stamped
a ruling paper slides under them

beats.say: The engineer of record argued that it was common practice to leave connections to the fabricator. Whose job was the joint?

params.place: the engineers' office, a drawing between two desks

moments.what: two desks, one at each side of the frame
the joint drawing slides between them
it stops in the gap, a question mark over it

beats.say: In {fact8}, the American Society of Civil Engineers answered: the engineer of record is responsible for the design of every steel connection.

params.place: the society's policy statement on the desk

moments.what: a policy card slides onto the desk, the year in yellow
the joint drawing slides to the engineer's side
the words ENGINEER OF RECORD type on
the joint ticks green

beats.say: Since then, the engineer of record answers for every connection, and a change to one is meant to be checked before it is built.

params.place: a change request loop drawn round the joint

moments.what: a change request leaves the shop
it travels to the engineer's desk
a calculation stamps CHECKED
it returns to the shop

beats.say: Engineering students still study this joint. A rod, a nut, a washer, and one phone call.

params.place: the joint on a dark table, turning slowly

moments.what: the box beam joint turns slowly under a spotlight
the rod lights
the nut lights
the washer lights
a telephone cord coils into frame beside it

beats.say: So which link should have stopped it? The weak original joint, the phone call, the detailer, or the review and the seal?

params.place: the investigators' cause board

moments.what: the cause chain card list pins up
the original joint stamps FACTOR · NBS
the rod change stamps FACTOR · NBS
the detailer stamps AS REPORTED
the review and seal stamp AS REPORTED; a yellow line underlines the board

params.cta: Which link should have stopped it?
params.assumption: From the National Bureau of Standards walkway investigation and ASCE. The reconstructions are not actual footage.

references.what: the walkway itself in 3D on a dark ground, an arrow and a few heavy words
three stacked heavy words beside the subject
the intended and the built connection side by side, a tick and a cross, two heavy words

thumbnails.pattern: the detail as designed beside the detail as built, a tick and a cross, two heavy words

references.what: the intended and the built connection side by side, a tick and a cross, two heavy words
the walkway itself in 3D on a dark ground, an arrow and a few heavy words
three stacked heavy words beside the subject

thumbnails.why: Clear at phone size, but its split frame with a tick and a cross sits too close to the 1.13M Deconstructed thumbnail beside it, and it is a flat drawing where the recipe asks for our 3D.

thumbnails.pattern: heavy serious type over one wide picture of the atrium

references.what: huge spaced serious type over one wide picture of the atrium
big serious serif type over one picture of the scene
three stacked heavy words beside the subject

thumbnails.why: Serious type over the atrium like the 1.2M Brick Immortar thumbnail, but the atrium reads pale and the sagging walkway is not clear enough to stop a scroll.
